To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned, sequenced, and characterized a novel streptocococcal protein, protein ZAG, that binds alpha 20M, serum albumin, IgG, and that is homologous to the previously characterized streptocococal protein G.
the Streptococcus zoepidemicus plasma protein receptor, protein ZAG, binds alpha 2M and IgG, and that the binding of these ligands is mediated by distinct domains.

the plasma protein receptor of S. zooepdemicus, termed protein ZA, has an IgG-binding profile similar to that of the streptocococcal protein receptor type III, and an alpha 2M- and albumin-binding profile similar to those of the streptcoccal plasma protein receptors type II and protein G, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of a gene encoding an IgG- and alpha 2M- and albumin-binding cell surface protein in S. zooepicdemicus.
the identification of a novel plasma protein receptor in S. zooepicemicus that is a member of the protein G superfamily.
a plasma protein receptor that has a modular structure with different domains for binding to different plasma proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein ZAG is a protein G-related cell-surface protein that is capable of binding alpha 2M and albumin and that is involved in the binding of IgG.
protein ZAG is the first example of a plasma protein receptor with a unique binding specificity in streptococi.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the alpha 2-macro-globulin-binding activity of protein ZAG and the streptococ- cal protein receptors is mediated by a domain with a unique amino acid sequence.
